note: 30 hand-labelled explain-back sentences over fixtures/sample-notes.md (PLAN §4.5, T-11). 15 GROUNDED (5 near-verbatim, 5 light paraphrase, 5 heavy paraphrase) and 15 INVENTED (5 plausible-true-but-absent, 5 wrong-number, 4 off-topic, 1 semantic-swap). Margin above is pre-registered before this set was run against core/ledger.js and is never adjusted to fit the result; OVERLAP_THRESHOLD in core/constants.js is untouched by this fixture. Two rows are pre-registered as expected false results because the Ledger only checks lexical overlap and exact numbers, never meaning: 'doubles-vs-increases' (DECISIONS 2026-08-25 01:50) is a wrong-number-shaped miss with no number in it, and one heavy-paraphrase row is a true statement reworded far enough from any single note line to fall under OVERLAP_THRESHOLD. Both misses are recorded here, not tuned away.

cases.text: Mature mammalian red blood cells have no mitochondria at all.
cases.label: GROUNDED
cases.why: Copied verbatim from the notes.

cases.text: Glucose is split into two pyruvate molecules.
cases.label: GROUNDED
cases.why: Copied verbatim from the notes.

cases.text: Oxygen is the final electron acceptor and is reduced to water.
cases.label: GROUNDED
cases.why: Copied verbatim from the notes.

cases.text: The chemiosmotic hypothesis was proposed in 1961.
cases.label: GROUNDED
cases.why: Copied verbatim from the notes, number intact.

cases.text: Each turn of the cycle produces 3 NADH, 1 FADH2 and 1 GTP.
cases.label: GROUNDED
cases.why: Near-verbatim, all three numbers intact.

cases.text: The mitochondrion word was coined by Carl Benda back in 1898.
cases.label: GROUNDED
cases.why: Word order and a filler word ('back') changed, same fact and number.

cases.text: Cristae increase the surface area of the inner membrane.
cases.label: GROUNDED
cases.why: Restates the cristae/surface-area line without changing any word that carries meaning.

cases.text: Protons are pumped into the intermembrane space as electrons move down the chain.
cases.label: GROUNDED
cases.why: Passive-voice rewrite of the electron-transport-chain sentence, same claim.

cases.text: The human mitochondrial genome contains 16,569 base pairs.
cases.label: GROUNDED
cases.why: Synonym swap ('contains' for 'is'), number intact.

cases.text: Pyruvate is converted to acetyl-CoA when it enters the matrix, releasing CO2.
cases.label: GROUNDED
cases.why: Clause order swapped, same fact.

cases.text: Since red blood cells in mammals lack mitochondria entirely, they rely solely on glycolysis for energy.
cases.label: GROUNDED
cases.why: True statement combining two adjacent note sentences (no mitochondria; glycolysis alone), reworded far enough that it may miss the overlap bar against any single note line — a known stress case for the align step, not tuned around.

cases.text: ATP synthase makes one ATP molecule for every three protons passing through it.
cases.label: GROUNDED
cases.why: Fully reworded restatement of the synthase 1-ATP-per-3-protons line, numbers intact.

cases.text: FADH2 yields less ATP than NADH because it bypasses complex I, resulting in fewer protons pumped.
cases.label: GROUNDED
cases.why: Reworded restatement of the FADH2/complex-I sentence.

cases.text: Because pyruvate can't get into the mitochondrion during fermentation, the ATP yield stays at the glycolysis figure.
cases.label: GROUNDED
cases.why: Reworded restatement of the fermentation sentence.

cases.text: The outer membrane's porins allow small molecules to pass through it.
cases.label: GROUNDED
cases.why: Reworded restatement of the outer-membrane/porins line.

cases.text: The mitochondrial genome is inherited exclusively from the mother.
cases.label: INVENTED
cases.why: True in general biology, never stated in these notes.

cases.text: Mitochondria are thought to have originated from ancient bacteria through endosymbiosis.
cases.label: INVENTED
cases.why: Plausible textbook fact absent from this notes file.

cases.text: Cyanide poisoning blocks the electron transport chain at complex IV.
cases.label: INVENTED
cases.why: True but never mentioned; notes name complex I only.

cases.text: Brown fat contains many mitochondria to generate heat instead of ATP.
cases.label: INVENTED
cases.why: True but off the notes entirely.

cases.text: Mitochondrial dysfunction is linked to Parkinson's disease and other neurodegenerative disorders.
cases.label: INVENTED
cases.why: True but off the notes entirely.

cases.text: The word mitochondrion was coined by Carl Benda in 1902.
cases.label: INVENTED
cases.why: Real fact, year changed from 1898 to 1902.

cases.text: A typical mitochondrion has a cross-section of about 5 to 8 square micrometres.
cases.label: INVENTED
cases.why: Real fact, range changed from 0.75-3 to 5-8.

cases.text: The human mitochondrial genome is 15,000 base pairs long.
cases.label: INVENTED
cases.why: Real fact, base-pair count changed from 16,569 to 15,000.

cases.text: The chemiosmotic hypothesis was proposed in 1965.
cases.label: INVENTED
cases.why: Real fact, year changed from 1961 to 1965.

cases.text: Peter Mitchell was awarded the Nobel Prize in Chemistry in 1985 for it.
cases.label: INVENTED
cases.why: Real fact, year changed from 1978 to 1985.

cases.text: Photosynthesis converts light energy into chemical energy stored in glucose.
cases.label: INVENTED
cases.why: Different biology topic, not covered by these notes.

cases.text: DNA replication occurs during the S phase of the cell cycle.
cases.label: INVENTED
cases.why: Different biology topic, not covered by these notes.

cases.text: The pancreas secretes insulin to regulate blood sugar levels.
cases.label: INVENTED
cases.why: Different biology topic, not covered by these notes.

cases.text: Osmosis is the movement of water across a semipermeable membrane.
cases.label: INVENTED
cases.why: Shares the word 'membrane' with several note lines but is a different topic entirely.

cases.text: Cristae double the surface area of the inner membrane.
cases.label: INVENTED
cases.why: The notes say cristae increase surface area, never that they double it — a specific, wrong quantitative claim with no digit in it. The Ledger has no reason code for a meaning-changing word swap and is pre-registered here as an expected false pass (DECISIONS 2026-08-25 01:50): this is the honest limit of a lexical-overlap check, not a bug to fix by tuning the threshold.
